chunks: And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from ‘Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Nahik, from Abu ‘Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “And We gave them both refuge on a mound, where there was rest and security, watered by a spring.” He said, “The mound is Najaf of Kufah, and the spring is the Euphrates.”

key_terms.رَبْوَةٍ: A high mound or elevated place of refuge
key_terms.مَعِينٍ: A flowing spring or source of water
key_terms.نَجَفُ الْكُوفَةِ: Najaf, a city near Kufah in Iraq

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Najaf and the Euphrates River in the interpretation of Surah Al-A'raf 7:65?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a specific exegetical interpretation linking the Quranic description of Prophet Hud’s refuge to the sacred geography of Iraq. He identifies the 'mound' (rabwah) as Najaf in Kufah and the 'spring' (ma'in) as the Euphrates River, thereby elevating these sites as places of divine provision and spiritual shelter. This interpretation underscores the enduring significance of the Euphrates in Shia tradition as a source of both physical sustenance and ritual purity.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from Sulaymān ibn Nahīk, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) explained the verse, “And we gave them both refuge on a mound, where there was rest and security, watered by a spring” [23:50].
He (the Imam (a.s.)) said, “Mound’ refers to Najaf of Kūfah and ‘spring’ refers to the Euphrates (River).”
